blocks.title: See and drive the iOS Simulator without leaving the conversation
blocks.description: Build Apple Apps puts a live iOS Simulator in the activity panel. The AI builds, installs and launches your app and checks the result with screenshots and logs, while you watch and tap through it on the same device.

showcase.user_prompt: Run the app and check whether the Settings screen looks right in dark mode.
showcase.assistant_reply: Built and installed on iPhone 17 Pro, switched to dark mode and deep-linked to Settings. The live screen is in the panel on the right; tap through it to try the flow yourself.

items.title: Live mirroring
items.description: Watch the simulator screen in the activity panel instead of switching to Simulator.app.

items.title: One device, shared
items.description: Tap, swipe and type in the panel while the AI builds and runs on the same simulator.

items.title: Checks its own work
items.description: After each change the AI rebuilds, relaunches and looks at a screenshot and the logs before reporting back.

items.title: Built-in development guide
items.description: SwiftUI component patterns, Liquid Glass adoption and performance audits load only when a task needs them.

items.title: Build-to-run loop
items.description: Building, installing, launching, deep links and simulated push notifications happen in one flow.

blocks.title: Compared with letting the AI run Xcode on its own

left.title: Command line only
items: Results are guessed from build logs

right.title: With Build Apple Apps
items: You see the screen right after each change
The AI checks its work with screenshots and logs
You can try the app on the same device at any time

items.title: Install Xcode and a simulator runtime
items.description: The plugin needs a Mac with Apple Silicon and uses the simulators you already have in Xcode.

items.title: Install and enable Build Apple Apps
items.description: Approve the requested permissions. The plugin runs the open-source serve-sim preview through Vetta's built-in Node runtime, on a local port only — nothing else to install.

items.title: Open an Xcode or SwiftPM project
items.description: The Simulator tab appears in the activity panel. The first start downloads serve-sim and can take a minute. Then ask the AI to build and run your app.

blocks.content: With Xcode 27, typing into the simulator from the panel needs the simulator window visible in Device Hub, and Vetta allowed under System Settings → Privacy & Security → Accessibility. Taps and swipes work without it.
